environment.description: Laravel 10.x application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB with session management delegated to a Redis-backed custom session handler. The infrastructure uses a credential rotation daemon (vault-agent sidecar) that cycles the APP_KEY and re-encrypts active session payloads every 60 seconds via a Lua script on the Redis cluster. Sessions are bound to a composite fingerprint (IP + User-Agent hash stored in the encrypted session payload). The ALB has a listener rule that inspects the Origin header and drops requests where Origin does not match the registered application FQDN (app.internal.corp) — implemented as a fixed-response 403 rule with priority 1 before the default forward rule. Additionally, the Redis session store uses a sliding-window token: each session record includes a monotonic 'seq' counter incremented on every authenticated request, and the session middleware rejects requests where the presented session seq is stale (differs by more than 1 from server-side seq), effectively making stolen session cookies expire within one request cycle even if somehow obtained.
